absent: Value and storage of profiling support flag, enable and compression switches and early callback pointer, including defaults and all writers.
Numeric values of tracking bypass flag, high memory, nowait, this node, no memalloc, account, nowarn and default slab allocation flags.
Definitions and values of proc report name, tag section name, debug and module configuration options and module tag helpers.
Behaviour of profiling shutdown, tag type registration, proc creation, module tag memory reserve and free, module load and replace, and proc and sysctl helpers.
Layouts of tag, type descriptor, tag reference, handle and page extension operations and helpers to get, put, update, clear and empty references.
Meanings of init, initdata, ref and init memblock attributes and boot versus runtime lifetime guarantees.
Values of possible processor count, maximum nodes, unassigned node sentinel, possible node map, node count storage, global processor masks and boot mask allocation.
Use of stored emulation string, distance algorithm, processor to node storage, and first chunk alloc, free, build info, setup chunk and free info helpers.
Values of percpu reserves, page size, cache bytes, total virtual space and address and frame number helpers and percpu tables.
Implementations of boot block alloc, reserved range removal, reserved area release, address translation, page handles, frame validity and slab availability test.
Layouts of leak object, pool, cache and locks and helpers to find and remove, link, delete, blacklist and prepare backtrace plus memory and task primitives.

Layouts of slab cache, slab and allocation context and helpers for pre and post hooks, debug alloc, strict policy, per processor cache, partial and new slab paths, out of memory report, user tracking, stats and pointer checks.
Exact error numbers, log levels and trace event formats for all reported paths.

findings.text: Exported profiling interfaces include early frame registration callable from boot allocation paths and a page extension operations descriptor consumed by page extension core plus a function pointer type for early callbacks and a macro wrapper that adds allocation hooks around the internal page allocator.

Exported NUMA interfaces include global off flag, per node mask storage, mask query, processor add and remove, node clearing for a processor, stored info publish, early mapping and early query, per processor offset table and area setup, plus node count setup and emulation command capture.

Exported low level memory interfaces include embedded first chunk creation for percpu, virtual and physical boot memory release, physical ignore and partial free hooks for leak tracking, and unprofiled slab cache allocation.

Early tracking node is a singly linked fixed capacity record. Member next chains to predecessor. Member count is atomic occupancy. Member pfns is trailing frame number storage. Capacity equals one page minus header divided by one number.
ABI virtual memory group vm holds mem_profiling with mode 0644 and mem_profiling_compressed with mode 0444.
ABI boot keywords are never for full profiling disable, compressed for compressed mode, off for NUMA disable, and fake followed by equals for emulation string.
ABI NUMA log prefix is the word NUMA followed by colon and space.
ABI tracking node capacity is page size minus node header size divided by size of one frame number.

Boot parameter handler decides early profiling support and mode. It rejects empty input, treats a full disable keyword as shutdown of support, otherwise accepts a boolean toggle plus optional compression keyword, announces the chosen mode, then aligns runtime enable and compression switches with parsed values, leaving them unchanged when already matching.

Late tag initialization first attempts virtual memory sysctl registration, with one build variant doing nothing. When global support is absent it logs and succeeds. Otherwise it creates a proc report with mode 0400, reserves module tag address space, registers the tag type with section name and object size plus module callbacks when modules are enabled, and on any failure releases prior resources, shuts down profiling and returns the error.

NUMA early parameter handler rejects null input, sets a global off flag when the option starts with the off keyword, and forwards fake prefixed strings to the emulation parser which stores the remainder for later use.

Node mask setup derives node count from highest possible node when still at maximum, aborts with error log on oversized count, then allocates and clears one mask per node. Percpu setup prefers embed allocation with module and dynamic reserves and NUMA aware callbacks, falls back to page allocation on failure or when embed was not chosen, halts on total failure, then computes each per processor offset as global delta from percpu base to static start plus per unit displacement.

Runtime toggle handler passes reads to the static key helper. Writes without user memory succeed immediately to absorb early boot replay. Writes while debugging support is compiled in are denied. Writes while global support is off are rejected. Remaining writes delegate to the static key helper.
Compressed mode makes per page tagging need false and makes early registration dispatch and handover no operation, leaving no early per frame state regardless of support flag.
Allocations marked as tracking internal never enter early registration, preventing self recursion from pages that back the tracking nodes themselves.

Processor to node mapping starts unassigned for every possible processor. Mask query returns all processor mask for unassigned node, none mask for out of range node, online mask when per node mask is missing, otherwise the stored per node mask, warning on the two degraded cases. Early node query returns the stored mapping entry.

Membership update ignores unassigned processors, otherwise sets or clears the bit in the owning node mask. Add and remove wrap the two directions. Clearing also resets the processor node to unassigned. Storing publishes the mapped node to per processor state. Early mapping clamps negative oversized or NUMA off requests to zero, records the choice, and immediately publishes zero for the boot processor.

Boot memory release ignores null virtual pointers, translates virtual to physical, emits debug trace, informs leak tracking of partial release, removes the range from reserved set only before slab is usable or when the architecture retains records, and releases pages to the page allocator only after slab is usable.

Preferred node slow path never mutates caller flags. It derives a constrained trial set with waiting suppressed and this node restriction for the first attempt, then restores original flags for the second attempt. Each attempt seeks partial slabs before creating a new slab.

Unprofiled cache allocation builds context from caller return address, cache object size and default flags, delegates to node allocation with no node preference, then traces. Node allocation runs a pre hook that may reject, tries a debug allocator that short circuits on hit, normalizes node through strict policy, attempts per processor cache, falls back to slow path on miss, conditionally clears embedded free pointer, then runs a post hook that may null the result. Sanitization zeroes one pointer sized field at cache offset only when init on free is requested, an object exists, and the pointer lives inside the object.

Tracker object creation initializes list and hash links, raw lock, use count to one, zeroed excess and scan state and checksum sentinel, captures process identity and command name with best effort copy, using distinct identities for hard interrupt, soft interrupt and process contexts, and prepares a backtrace handle.

Tracker object supply prefers dedicated slab cache with nested mask, then locked freelist, then static reserve, otherwise warns once about exhaustion and returns null. Slab miss without pool entry yields null.
Physical ignore and partial free hooks emit debug output and act only when tracking is enabled, delegating to blacklisting and object split deletion respectively.

Early registration pointer is read under read side critical section and retired by null publication followed by grace period wait, ensuring no concurrent inserter still dereferences the old target before pools are reclaimed.

Leak tracker pool and object tree are guarded by irq saving raw spinlock held across freelist removal, covering object lookup and remainder linkage, with spare preallocation and original destruction performed outside. Partial deletion preallocates two spares, links left and right remainders when non empty, destroys the original or warns in debug builds when absent, and returns unused spares.

Early pool publication and occupancy use single volatile load plus compare exchanges on head pointer and counter with no sleeping locks, relying on retry loops for concurrent publishers. Tracking nodes are allocated as single high memory pages on local memory and marked to bypass tagging, with failure warned once and the number dropped.

Profiling moves from unsupported to supported with independent enable and compression switches. Full disable keyword forces unsupported and off. Otherwise support is on and switches follow parsed values. Runtime toggle is allowed only when supported and not debugging. Late init shuts down on any resource failure.

Early collection starts with null head, grows by prepending new nodes when missing or full, dispatches through a live pointer that may be absent, then transitions to retired by nulling the pointer, waiting for readers, draining each pooled number with validity and tag checks that preserve already valid tags and reset others to empty, and freeing each pool page after clearing its own tag. One build variant makes handover empty and page extension init only invokes handover.

Slow path cycles through opportunistic this node partial, opportunistic new slab, full partial, full new slab, then success, downgraded retry, spinning retry or failure. Tiny and debug caches take singly from a fresh slab, other caches bulk take one and return immediately. Slow path and new slab events are counted and user tracking is recorded when enabled.

Embed creation builds allocation info from reserves and atom size, reserves a group pointer array from boot allocator, reserves one contiguous block per group on a representative processor while ignoring the ranges for leak tracking, derives span from lowest base and highest group, warns and optionally fails when span exceeds three quarters of virtual space, copies static data into assigned units while freeing unused units and tails, records per group base offsets, publishes the chunk, and on failure releases all group blocks and the pointer array.
If the page backing a new tracking node cannot be allocated, the frame number is silently dropped after a one time warning, leaving that early allocation untracked and risking undercount.

Between validity check and empty marking there is an accepted small race where a concurrent reallocation could gain a valid tag that then gets overwritten with empty. The design tolerates this in debug only code rather than adding atomic compare exchange.
Excessive group span beyond most of virtual space warns and, where a fallback exists, fails the embed path to allow page based fallback. Total inability to establish percpu storage halts boot.
Exhaustion of slab cache and static reserve yields null tracker objects, warns once, and disables leak tracking entirely on the creation path, silently losing later leak coverage.
Persistent inability to obtain partial or new slab reports out of memory and returns null. Non spinning contexts fail immediately rather than risk unbounded retry.

Oversized node count aborts mask setup with error log leaving masks uninitialized. Invalid node queries and missing per node masks trigger warnings and substitute safe global masks, potentially masking configuration errors.
